title: How to Plan for Retirement When You Have No 401(k) Access
description: Building a 'DIY' pension using IRAs, HSAs, and Taxable Accounts.
content:
About 50% of the US workforce has no access to a workplace retirement plan. If you work for a small business, are self-employed, or work part-time, you don't have the easy path of payroll deductions and employer matches. You must build your own infrastructure. The good news is that you can often build a better, lower-cost portfolio on your own than in a high-fee corporate plan. This guide maps the 'DIY' path to financial independence.

Key Takeaways

  • The IRA Foundation: Your first bucket is the IRA (Individual Retirement Account). You can contribute $7,000/year. Automate this from your bank account to mimic a paycheck deduction.
  • Taxable is Fine: Once the IRA is full, you must use a Taxable Brokerage account. While it lacks tax deductions, it offers total liquidity and low capital gains tax rates. It is not a bad place to save.
  • HSA as Super-IRA: If you buy your own insurance on the Marketplace, choose an HDHP to unlock the HSA. This gives you a $4,300 tax deduction that you otherwise miss without a 401(k).
  • The Saver's Credit: Low-to-moderate income earners can get a tax credit (up to $1,000) just for contributing to an IRA. It is the government's version of a 'match'.

Why It Matters (US Context)

The barrier to entry for DIY investing is zero. Fidelity, Schwab, and Vanguard allow you to open IRAs for free. You do not need an employer to grant you permission to save.

The Contribution Waterfall

Without a 401(k), you fill buckets in this order.

Bucket 1: The Deductible IRA ($7,000)

Why: Since you have no workplace plan, you can deduct 100% of your Traditional IRA contributions regardless of income. This lowers your tax bill immediately.

Alternative: Roth IRA if your income is low and you want tax-free growth.

Bucket 2: The HSA ($4,300)

Why: Reduces taxable income. Invest it for the long term.

Bucket 3: Tax-Efficient Brokerage (Unlimited)

Why: You ran out of tax shelters.
Strategy: Buy broad index ETFs (VTI/VXUS). They generate very little tax drag.
Benefit: This money is accessible at any age. You are building a 'FIRE' fund by default.

Automation is the Boss

  1. Fake the Paycut: Calculate what 15% of your pay is. Set up an auto-transfer for that amount to occur the day after you get paid. You must create your own scarcity.
  2. Lobby the Boss: If you work for a small business, ask them to set up a SIMPLE IRA. It costs them almost nothing to administer and allows you to save $16,000/year with a match.
  3. The 'Tax Refund' Sweep: Since you aren't getting pre-tax payroll deductions, you might owe less tax or get a refund based on IRA deductions. Reinvest any tax savings immediately.
  4. Spousal 401(k): If you are married and your spouse has a plan, have them contribute double to their 401(k) to cover 'your share,' and use your income to pay household bills. Money is fungible.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I retire on just $7,000/year?

Likely not. $7k/yr over 30 years is ~$700,000. That helps, but you probably need more. You must save in a taxable account beyond the IRA limit.

Is a taxable account bad?

No. You pay Capital Gains tax (0-15-20%), which is lower than Income Tax. It is a very efficient way to build wealth, just with less upfront breaks.

What is a myRA?

A discontinued government program. Do not look for it. Use a private IRA at a brokerage instead.
